Review: Spotify's desktop app stopped producing audio on my Mac while all other audio worked normally. I contacted support, where a bot (which refused to identify itself as such) declined a refund for a service that was not functioning, offered no compensation, and presented only two options: perform an indefinite amount of unpaid labor troubleshooting, or cancel moving forward. When I asked to speak with a human agent, I was denied. When I indicated I would send the chat transcript to the FTC and our state's AG office, I was transferred to a human agent.The human agent offered no meaningful support, including suggested a fix of reinstalling the app, did not work. The reinstall does not clear a hidden local config directory that was the actual source of the problem. I resolved the issue myself after ending the support session and spending considerable individual effort.If you have the same problem (desktop app silent, browser or other audio works fine), quit Spotify, open Terminal, run rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Spotify, and relaunch. You will need to log in again, but it resets the corrupted audio routing config that a normal reinstall leaves in place.A company that charges $23.53/month for a family plan should be able to diagnose its own software failures, not recite refund policy while its product sits broken.

Review: The free version works fine for about five seconds until you try to loop songs. On the mobile app especially, songs on the free version cannot be looped properly. I've tried adding playlists with one song entered, over, and over, and over again. However, if you're like me, and you like listening to YOUR music, and not the recommended songs that Spotify forces on you, you're eventually going to run into the problem where it says, "Cannot queue this content." In fact, even if you go to the search bar and pick a song there, it will not play that song. It will play another "recommended song." That is not what a user wants! They want to listen to their music that they CHOOSE. Not a recommended song. I will say, giving some credit to Spotify here, adding a single song on a playlist does work in looping it. However, this is largely counteracted with Spotify mixing in recommended songs in that playlist due to "Smart Shuffle." Some people just want to loop their music without having to pay for a subscription.Another issue that I have found incredibly annoying are the "Made For You" playlists. Some people may find these just fine. Even I have a "Made For You" playlist that I listen to regularly. My only issue that I have with those playlists is the fact that you can't delete them. C'mon, at least let us users be able to have an option to remove these from our home screens so it's not cluttered up with 5 or 6 playlists we'll never listen too. At least for me, a lot of these playlists are single songs that I listened to because I accidentally hit a playlist instead of a song. I'll admit, yes that is my fault for not reading, but at least give us the option to remove unwanted playlists, even if they are made for us.Oh, and don't get me started with, what I like to call, "Undead Playlists." Once upon a time, a younger me made a playlist. I listened to it, enjoyed it, but music taste changes (something that I don't think Spotify really considers unless you're actively "removing from taste profile"), so now an older me tried deleting that playlist. And it deleted...for three seconds. I closed and reopened the app the next day, and what do you know? There it is, an empty playlist, taking up space, undelete-able. And I can't remove it to this day. This is something super annoying, ruining the user experience, that could be fixed with a simple feature of being able to remove unwanted playlists from your homepage!I want to be able to freely skip songs that I don't want to listen to, instead of just 6 an hour. I want to be able to listen to whatever song I want, when I want, however many times I choose to. I want to be able to clear unwanted playlists from my homepage. Above all, I want these features available on free version of the Spotify app. Users should NOT be forced to pay for a subscription just to have a good user experience. Lot of us don't have the option to pay for a subscription whatsoever. As far as I'm aware, the free trial doesn't even activate on the mobile app, at least, it doesn't for me.The only, only downside that the free version should be the adds. Whether a user is paying for a subscription, or a user is interrupted with adds, Spotify will make money either way.Fix the user experience for free users. Stop breaking the free version of Spotify just to get users to pay for a $12.99 subscription.I hope you consider this message, and have a wonderful day.

Review: Spotify is a very strong platform from a listener’s perspective: it is convenient, easy to use, offers a huge music library, and has become one of the main places where people discover and listen to music.From the perspective of an independent artist, however, my experience is much more disappointing. Spotify gives the impression of reach and visibility, but in practice very little of that turns into real support or sustainable growth. Streams generate extremely low income, older achievements quickly lose visibility, follower numbers feel unstable, and without additional marketing money almost nothing happens.The problem is not Spotify alone, but the whole system around it. Artists create the music, invest time, money and energy, while platforms, distributors, labels and marketing services benefit far more from the structure. For independent musicians, this can easily become frustrating: you keep working, hoping and investing, but the system rarely gives much back.For listeners, Spotify is excellent. For independent artists, it can be deeply discouraging, unfair and exhausting.
